entries.title: Rossella Biscotti, Le teste in oggetto
text: Five bronze heads of Mussolini and King Vittorio Emanuele III, made by Giovanni Prini and Domenico Rambelli for the Rome world's fair of 1942 and never shown: the fair was cancelled. Rossella Biscotti and Kevin van Braak found them in a storeroom at EUR and in 2009 set them on pallets on a gallery floor for one week.
Nothing is done to them but the move, out of storage and onto freight pallets. Museion in Bolzano holds a work of the same title of 2015, in silicone and acrylic resin.
facts: Named by the author on 13 November 2026 as 'Teste in oggetto' (notes, section added that day).

Confirmed by https://nomasfoundation.com/en/mostre/rossella-biscotti-le-teste-in-oggetto/: 'five bronze sculptures portraying the heads of King Victor Emmanuel III and Benito Mussolini', by the sculptors Giovanni Prini and Domenico Rambelli, made for the 1942 Universal Exhibition of Rome (E42/EUR), which was cancelled; never shown to the public.

Same page: found during archive research in Rome by Rossella Biscotti and Kevin van Braak; moved from the storage rooms of the Palazzo degli Uffici at EUR; installed at Nomas Foundation for one week, then a large photograph and documents; exhibition 4 April to 18 May 2009, curated by Maria Rosa Sossai, in collaboration with EUR S.p.A.

Museion's record on Google Arts & Culture (https://artsandculture.google.com/asset/le-teste-in-oggetto/7gFz_EQwXZHbsw): 'Le Teste in Oggetto', Rossella Biscotti, 2015, 'Silicone RTV-2/118, ceramic-like acrylic resin (on 2 Euro-palletts)', 'w100 x h118 x d50 cm (each)', Museion Collection, photo Nicolò Degiorgis.
How the 2015 Museion work relates to the bronzes of 2009 is not stated on either page; that it is a cast or a later version is an inference from title and materials [INF].
Museion showed Biscotti's exhibition 'The future can only be for ghosts' from 31 January to 25 May 2015 (search result for Museion's Google Arts story, page not opened) [SS].

Seen in the image: four monumental dark bronze heads, each on a wooden pallet on a concrete floor in a white room; two wear helmets with a crest, two are bare-headed and seen from the side and the back.

images.caption: Rossella Biscotti, The Heads in Question, installation view, Nomas Foundation, Rome, 2009. Photo: Ela Bialkowska. © the artist and photographer; from the foundation's page.

entries.title: Francesco Arena, Trittico 57
text: Made for Museion, Bolzano, 2012. Three slabs of travertine, the same size and stone as the three added in 1957 to complete Hans Piffrader's frieze of Mussolini on horseback on the Casa del Fascio. Into them Arena sandblasted the letter with which Italo Calvino left the Communist Party that same year, turned into Morse code.
The year a missing piece was fixed to a dictator's image, a writer detached himself from his party. The letter is there as dots and dashes, worn by the sandblaster as time wears an inscription.
facts: Named by the author on 13 November 2026 as 'Francesco Arena Museion' (notes, section added that day).

Confirmed by https://museion.it/en/exhibitions/75-trittico-57: exhibition 'Trittico 57', Francesco Arena, Museion, 30 March to 6 May 2012; three slabs of travertine arranged as a triptych, the same size and material as the slabs used in 1957 to complete Hans Piffrader's frieze.

Same page: the frieze was made in 1943 for the Casa Littoria, today Bolzano's Finance Offices, and shows Mussolini on horseback; during a visit by President Giovanni Gronchi it was decided to finish it, and three missing slabs were added.

Same page: on 7 August 1957 Italo Calvino publicly left the Italian Communist Party with a letter in L'Unità; Arena carved that letter into the slabs translated into Morse code, with a sandblaster; the page compares this to time wearing down ancient inscriptions, and says the rhythm of dots and dashes matters more to him than the literal meaning.
The page was read through a summary; its wording is paraphrased here, not quoted.
A German-language report says the sandblasting makes the letters hard to read (stol.it, search result only) [SS].
The frieze itself and the Arendt sentence set across it in 2017 are rows 5.20 to 5.24 of this library (notes 05, §4).

Seen in the image: a person in a white protective suit and green hood sandblasting a pale stone slab propped against a wall in a yard, the slab's surface patchy and eroded; a blasting pot with hoses, pallets with crates, two steel tanks and a house behind.

images.caption: Francesco Arena, Trittico 57, 2012: a slab being sandblasted. Photograph from Museion's exhibition page; credit not stated.

entries.title: Gianni Pettena, Secoli e millenni
text: A pencil drawing from a series of 2014 by Gianni Pettena, born in Bolzano in 1940: the Monument to Victory as a ruin. The columns stand broken, the steps are cracked and strewn with blocks, brush closes in from both sides, and the mountains behind are unchanged. The title sets centuries against millennia.

It is shown by courtesy of the artist and Museion. The university's research group on Bolzano's fascist legacy used this sheet in 2024 to announce its seminar “Inhabited Dissonance. Bozen-Bolzano 1922-2024”.
facts: Named by the author on 13 November 2026 as 'Secoli e millenni di Pettena' (notes, section added that day).

Confirmed by https://www.unibz.it/en/events/inhabited-dissonance-bozen-bolzano-1922-2: image caption 'Gianni Pettena, from the series “Secoli e Millenni”, 2014. Courtesy of the artist and of Museion – Museum of Modern and Contemporary Art Bolzano Bozen'; the image's alternative text is 'Monument to Victory'.

Same page: the seminar 'Inhabited Dissonance. Bozen-Bolzano 1922-2024', 5 to 7 June 2024, Faculty of Design and Art of the Free University of Bozen-Bolzano, by the working group of the research project 'Curating Bozen-Bolzano Fascist Legacy. A sustainable approach to a city's dissonant heritage' (CuFa), led by Roberto Gigliotti with Andrea Di Michele and Waltraud Kofler Engl; results to be shown at the Galleria Civica in April 2025.

Confirmed by https://kunstmeranoarte.org/en/exhibitions/gianni-pettena-natural-architecture-en: 'Gianni Pettena (born 1940 in Bolzano, lives in Florence)'; exhibition 'Natural architecture', 22 July to 24 September 2017, curated by Christiane Rekade; an image caption there reads 'Atta Unsar, 1973 / Secoli e millenni, 2014'.

Seen in the image: a pencil drawing on white paper of a pillared monument in ruins on a stepped base: two broken clusters of columns still carry fragments of the top, thinner broken columns stand between them, blocks lie on cracked steps, hatched vegetation rises at both sides, a town and mountains fill the background; a handwritten '4' at lower right.

images.caption: Gianni Pettena, from the series “Secoli e millenni”, 2014. Courtesy of the artist and Museion, Bolzano; from the university's event page.

entries.title: DAAR (Sandi Hilal and Alessandro Petti), Ente di Decolonizzazione – Borgo Rizza
text: Borgo Rizza is a rural settlement near Syracuse built in 1940 by the fascist agency for colonising the Sicilian estates. DAAR, the practice of Sandi Hilal and Alessandro Petti, made a scaled reproduction of the front of its main building and cut it into fifteen modules. Since 2022 people have sat on them to talk, in Naples, Berlin, Brussels and Venice.
Their word is to “profane” the architecture, to use it against itself. Golden Lion, Venice 2023. It is the kind of settlement the second report sets beside Bolzano's Semirurali.
facts: Named by the author on 13 November 2026 as 'Daar - decolonizing architecture, Petti' (notes, section added that day).

Confirmed by https://www.labiennale.org/en/architecture/2023/dangerous-liaisons/daar-alessandro-petti-and-sandi-hilal: 'Ente di Decolonizzazione – Borgo Rizza', DAAR's contribution to the Biennale Architettura 2023; it explores reappropriating, reusing and subverting fascist colonial architecture and its modernist legacy; Borgo Rizza, Syracuse, Sicily, built in 1940; the installation is a scaled reproduction of the façade of the village's main building, divided into fifteen multipurpose modules, used since May 2022 in conversations at the Mostra d'Oltremare in Naples, the Hansaviertel in Berlin and La Loge in Brussels; the page speaks of an attempt to 'profane' the settlement.

Confirmed by https://www.decolonizing.ps/site/?p=5105 (DAAR's own page, July 2022): 'Starting from the decomposition and recomposition of the facade of the Entity of Colonization'; the modules form 'an open discursive space'; the public is invited to 'reconsider critically the social, political and economic effect of fascist and colonial heritage'; modernist buildings 'need to be profaned, to be used against themselves, and open for new common uses'; 'Documentation: Pietro Onofri'.

DAAR's page names the 'Entity of Colonization of the Sicilian Latifundium' and dates it to 1940; its Italian name, Ente di Colonizzazione del Latifondo Siciliano (ECLS), is from a search result only [SS].

Confirmed by https://www.labiennale.org/en/news/awards-biennale-architettura-2023: 'Golden Lion for the best participant in the 18th Exhibition The Laboratory of the Future' to DAAR – Alessandro Petti and Sandi Hilal, 'for their long-standing commitment to deep political engagement with architectural and learning practices of decolonization' 'in Palestine and Europe'; ceremony on 20 May 2023.
DAAR stands for Decolonizing Architecture Art Research (search results) [SS]; the author's note has 'decolonizing architecture'.

The ECLS is not in this research's notes; the second report compares the Semirurali with the Pontine, Libyan, Ethiopian and Dodecanese settlements, not with the Sicilian ones (reports, 'Semirurali versus Libyan villages').

Seen in the image: about twenty-five people sitting in a ring on low blocks, white with red tops and sides, on a dark carpet outdoors; behind them a long basin of water between clipped hedges and umbrella pines, a tower block in the distance.

images.caption: DAAR, Ente di Decolonizzazione – Borgo Rizza, 2022: the modules in use outdoors. From DAAR's own page; credit not stated beside the picture (“Documentation: Pietro Onofri” on the page).
